Again he denied it with an oath, “I don’t know the man.”
After a little while those who stood by came and said to Peter, “Surely you are also one of them, for your speech makes you known.”
Then he began to curse and to swear, “I don’t know the man!” Immediately the rooster crowed.
Peter remembered the word which Jesus had said to him, “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” Then he went out and wept bitterly.
b: This passage portrays Peter's three denials of Jesus, which took place after Jesus was arrested. Under outside pressure and fear, Peter three times claimed that he did not know Jesus, the last time even swearing and cursing to prove his words. At the height of his denial the rooster crowed, and he suddenly remembered Jesus' earlier prophecy. Filled with deep remorse, he went outside alone and wept bitterly.

This event reflects the frailty and fear in human nature, and the tendency to abandon faith under extreme pressure. Peter's experience teaches us that even the most steadfast believer may fall in trial. Yet it also shows God's grace and forgiveness, since we know that Peter was later restored and became an important leader of the early church.

Through this passage God reminds us that He understands our weakness and failure. In our own lives, when we face temptation and challenge, God still gives us the opportunity to repent and to receive His favor again.
q: Think of a choice you once made under pressure. What did you learn from it? In future trials, how can you better rely on God rather than on your own strength?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Peter's experience that even in failure and weakness, Your grace is still sufficient. Help us, when we face trials and fear, to hold fast to our loyalty to You, and when we fall, to stand up bravely and return to Your embrace. We pray all this in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now when morning had come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death:
and they bound him, and led him away, and delivered him up to Pontius Pilate, the governor.
Then Judas, who betrayed him, when he saw that Jesus was condemned, felt remorse, and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
saying, “I have sinned in that I betrayed innocent blood.” But they said, “What is that to us? You see to it.”
He threw down the pieces of silver in the sanctuary, and departed. He went away and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the pieces of silver, and said, “It’s not lawful to put them into the treasury, since it is the price of blood.”
They took counsel, and bought the potter’s field with them, to bury strangers in.
Therefore that field was called “The Field of Blood” to this day.

Then that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying, “They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him upon whom a price had been set, whom some of the children of Israel priced,
and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord commanded me.”
b: This passage describes Jesus being delivered to the Roman governor Pilate, and the deep remorse and tragic end of Judas. Seeing that Jesus had been condemned, Judas was seized with extreme remorse and tried to return the thirty pieces of silver he had been paid for betraying Him, and in despair he finally took his own life. The money was used to buy the "Field of Blood" as a burial place for foreigners, fulfilling the prophecy of the prophet Jeremiah.

This passage shows the consequences of sin and the dilemma of repentance. Judas' actions reveal the inner struggle and spiritual collapse that greed and betrayal can bring. Although his remorse was real, he did not seek true forgiveness and redemption, but chose the path of despair to end his life.

What God shows us through this passage is that no matter how serious our mistakes, we should seek His forgiveness. True repentance is not only recognizing our wrongs; with God's help it also means walking the road toward reconciliation and renewal.
q: Have there been times in your life when you regretted a wrong choice? How did you deal with that regret? How can you seek renewal and restoration through the grace of Christ?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your word that each of us may fall into the temptation of sin. Help us recognize our sin and seek Your forgiveness. When we face temptation and challenge, let us remember to seek Your face, not through self-destruction, but through repentance and restoring our relationship with You. In the name of Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “So you say.”
When he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.
Then Pilate said to him, “Don’t you hear how many things they testify against you?”
He gave him no answer, not even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.
Now at the feast the governor was accustomed to release to the multitude one prisoner, whom they desired.
They had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.
When therefore they were gathered together, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus, who is called Christ?”
For he knew that because of envy they had delivered him up.
While he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered many things today in a dream because of him.”
Now the chief priests and the elders persuaded the multitudes to ask for Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
But the governor answered them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas!”
Pilate said to them, “What then shall I do to Jesus, who is called Christ?” They all said to him, “Let him be crucified!”
But the governor said, “Why? What evil has he done?” But they cried out exceedingly, saying, “Let him be crucified!”

So when Pilate saw that nothing was being gained, but rather that a disturbance was starting, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, “I am innocent of the blood of this righteous person. You see to it.”
All the people answered, “May his blood be on us, and on our children!”
Then he released to them Barabbas, but Jesus he flogged and delivered to be crucified.
b: This passage describes Jesus' trial before the Roman governor Pilate. Jesus was accused of being the King of the Jews, but under questioning He made almost no defense. Pilate tried to release Jesus because he could find no crime in Him. Yet, strongly influenced by the chief priests and elders, the people chose to have a criminal, Barabbas, released and demanded that Jesus be crucified. In the end Pilate washed his hands to show that he was not responsible for the blood of this righteous man, and handed Jesus over to be crucified.

The focus of this passage is to show the process of Jesus suffering though innocent, while revealing the weakness and cowardice of people in the face of moral and group pressure. Jesus' calm and firmness, along with Pilate's conflict, bring out a profound moral dilemma and a spiritual test.

Through this passage God reveals to us that truth and justice are often misunderstood and rejected in the world. The story of Jesus' suffering inspires us to hold on to faith and justice even in the midst of extreme injustice and persecution.
q: Think about your own life: have there been times when fear of what others would think kept you from standing on the side of justice? How can you better stand for truth and justice in the future?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, give us courage and wisdom, so that when we face injustice and challenge in life, we may hold fast to righteousness and truth. When temptation and pressure come, remind us that Your love and Your way are our guide forever. Help us to be witnesses of Your righteousness and love. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered the whole garrison together against him.
They stripped him, and put a scarlet robe on him.
They braided a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand; and they kneeled down before him, and mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They spat on him, and took the reed and struck him on the head.
When they had mocked him, they took the robe off him, and put his clothes on him, and led him away to crucify him.
b: This passage describes the mockery and torment Jesus suffered from the Roman soldiers. Before He was crucified, the soldiers subjected Him to extreme ridicule and humiliation. They put a scarlet robe on Him, a mocking symbol of kingship, and placed on His head a crown woven of thorns, which not only caused physical pain but also symbolized the weight of sin and human fallenness. All of this was done in mockery of Jesus' claim to be "the King of the Jews."

The heart of this passage is to reveal that Jesus' suffering was not only physical torture but also deep mental and emotional pain. Here Jesus showed immense patience and resolve; even in the face of extreme humiliation and pain, He persevered in completing the mission of redemption God had given Him.

Through this passage God shows us that even the Son of God did not escape the suffering of the world. This reminds us to seek God's face in suffering and to learn to keep our faith and dignity in adversity. Jesus' experience also encourages us, when we face trials and pain in life, to bear and overcome them bravely, and to find spiritual strength and growth in them.
q: Reflect on your attitude when you face insult or injustice. How have you responded? How can you better follow Jesus' example and respond to these challenges with love and forbearance?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for showing us, through Your Son Jesus Christ, what endurance and courage look like. When we face mockery, pain, or misunderstanding, give us strength to take Jesus as our example and to live out our faith steadily and with dignity. Help us see Your hand guiding us in every circumstance. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: As they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and they compelled him to go with them, that he might carry his cross.
When they came to a place called “Golgotha”, that is to say, “The place of a skull,”
they gave him sour wine to drink mixed with gall. When he had tasted it, he would not drink.
When they had crucified him, they divided his clothing among them, casting lots,
and they sat and watched him there.
They set up over his head the accusation against him written, “THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
Then there were two robbers crucified with him, one on his right hand and one on the left.
b: This passage describes Jesus carrying the cross and being crucified at Golgotha. As Jesus walked toward the place of His suffering, a man from Cyrene named Simon was compelled by the Roman soldiers to help carry the cross, showing the frailty and exhaustion of Jesus' humanity. When they came to "the place of the skull," Jesus refused the wine mixed with gall, a drug meant to ease pain, showing that He chose to face death fully conscious.

The soldiers divided Jesus' garments by casting lots, fulfilling a prophecy of the Old Testament and underscoring that every detail of Jesus' suffering was part of God's will. The sign over His head read, "This is Jesus, the King of the Jews," which was both a mockery of His identity and, unintentionally, a confirmation of His kingship. Jesus was also crucified between two criminals, symbolizing His suffering among sinners and showing that He paid the price for the sins of all humanity.

What God conveys to us through this passage is a profound message about sacrifice and redemption. Jesus' suffering and death were not an accident but the plan the Father set in order to save the world, especially sinners. It shows God's great love for humanity, in that He was willing to give the life of His only Son to bring about reconciliation between people and God.
q: In your life, how do you respond to the unconditional love and spirit of sacrifice Jesus demonstrated? What specific ways can help you follow Jesus more closely and be a blessing to those around you?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, we thank You that through the sacrifice of Your Son Jesus Christ You have shown unconditional love and supreme redemption. As we reflect on Jesus' suffering and sacrifice, help us experience this love more deeply and live it out in our daily lives. Draw our hearts closer to You and let us reflect the image of Christ more and more. In the name of Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads,
and saying, “You who destroy the temple, and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
Likewise the chief priests also mocking, with the scribes, the Pharisees, and the elders, said,
“He saved others, but he can’t save himself. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.
He trusts in God. Let God deliver him now, if he wants him; for he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’ ”
The robbers also who were crucified with him cast on him the same reproach.
b: This passage describes the mockery and humiliation Jesus endured on the cross. Passersby, the chief priests, scribes, elders, and even the robbers crucified with Him all taunted Jesus. They challenged Him that if He were truly the Son of God, He should be able to save Himself and come down. These taunts fully display humanity's ignorance of God's sacred purpose and misunderstanding of the truth.

Jesus' silence and endurance on the cross show His absolute submission to the Father's will, even in the face of tremendous pain and humiliation. It was not only the final test of His identity but also the perfect fulfillment of His mission: to atone for the sins of all humanity.

Through this passage God shows us that true strength sometimes lies in enduring rather than striking back, and that a true king sometimes chooses to display authority through humility and sacrifice. Jesus' suffering and death are the greatest demonstration of love for us, reminding us that no matter what challenge or pain we face, there is a greater plan within it.
q: Think back: when you meet injustice or mockery in life, how do you respond? Can you find the patience and perseverance you can learn from Jesus' suffering? How can you better practice this strength from the inside out in your daily life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for showing us, through the sacrifice of Your Son Jesus Christ on the cross, what true endurance and submission are. When we meet trials and difficulties in life, give us strength to face challenges following Jesus' example, and in every circumstance to seek and carry out Your will. In the name of Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?”  That is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
Some of them who stood there, when they heard it, said, “This man is calling Elijah.”
Immediately one of them ran, and took a sponge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him a drink.
The rest said, “Let him be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to save him.”
Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and yielded up his spirit.
Behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.
The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised;
and coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they entered into the holy city and appeared to many.
Now the centurion, and those who were with him watching Jesus, when they saw the earthquake, and the things that were done, feared exceedingly, saying, “Truly this was the Son of God.”
Many women were there watching from afar, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
b: This passage describes the final moments of Jesus' crucifixion. From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole land. In extreme agony Jesus cried out to God, quoting the opening of Psalm 22 to express His loneliness and sense of abandonment. When He cried out with a loud voice and finally breathed His last, not only did the earth shake, but the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, symbolizing the removal of the barrier between God and people. In addition, the tombs were opened and the bodies of many saints were raised, symbolizing the great significance of Jesus' death and His authority over life.

Jesus' death on the cross was not only a historical event but also a spiritual turning point, revealing God's plan of redemption for humanity. Through Jesus' death, God shows us how seriously He takes sin and how immeasurably He loves humanity. Jesus' cry shows that even the Son of God, in bearing the burden of human sin, experienced great psychological and emotional stress. God did not forsake Jesus; through His death and resurrection He accomplished the great plan of reconciling people with God.
q: When you feel lonely or abandoned in the low points of life, how do you find comfort and strength? How can you experience Jesus' presence and peace more deeply in your daily life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Your love for us and Your forgiveness of sin through the sacrifice of Your Son Jesus Christ. Help us understand the depth and breadth of this love, and let it inspire every step of our lives. Even in the darkest moments, let us remember that Jesus has overcome the world and given us eternal hope and comfort. In the name of Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When evening had come, a rich man from Arimathaea, named Joseph, who himself was also Jesus’ disciple came.
This man went to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate commanded the body to be given up.
Joseph took the body, and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock, and he rolled a great stone against the door of the tomb, and departed.
Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.
Now on the next day, which was the day after the Preparation Day, the chief priests and the Pharisees were gathered together to Pilate,
saying, “Sir, we remember what that deceiver said while he was still alive: ‘After three days I will rise again.’

Command therefore that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come at night and steal him away, and tell the people, ‘He is risen from the dead;’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”
Pilate said to them, “You have a guard. Go, make it as secure as you can.”
So they went with the guard and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone.
b: This passage records the burial of Jesus after His crucifixion. Joseph, a rich man from Arimathea and a secret disciple of Jesus, courageously asked Pilate for the body of Jesus. He laid Jesus in his own new tomb, showing his love and respect for Him. In addition, the chief priests and Pharisees expressed to Pilate their concern that Jesus' disciples might steal His body, and asked that the tomb be securely guarded to prevent a rumor that Jesus had risen.

The focus of this passage is Jesus' burial and the guarding of the tomb. These two actions not only made Jesus' resurrection verifiable but also show how seriously, and with what fear, the authorities took the prophecy of His resurrection. Jesus' death and burial are at the core of the Christian faith, foreshadowing the great redemptive significance of His death.

Through this passage God reveals to us that even in seemingly hopeless situations, His plan continues to unfold. Jesus' burial was not the end but an important part of the plan of redemption, paving the way for His resurrection.
q: When you face "deaths" and "endings" in life, how do you rely on the hope of Jesus' resurrection to restore confidence and strength? How can you show your faith in Christ's resurrection in your daily life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for revealing, through the death and burial of Jesus Christ, Your deep love and redemption for the world. Let us experience Your presence in our lives and still see Your work in difficulty. When we face trials and challenges, help us remember Jesus' sacrifice and the hope of His resurrection. In the name of Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
Behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from the sky, and came and rolled away the stone from the door, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
For fear of him, the guards shook, and became like dead men.
The angel answered the women, “Don’t be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus, who has been crucified.
He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said. Come, see the place where the Lord was lying.
Go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him.’ Behold, I have told you.”
They departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring his disciples word.
b: This passage describes the first morning after Jesus' resurrection, when two women, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary, came to Jesus' tomb. They witnessed an extraordinary miracle: an angel descended from heaven, there was an earthquake, and the stone was rolled away, with the angel sitting on it. The angel's appearance and words announced Jesus' resurrection to the women and instructed them to go and tell the other disciples this good news.

The core message of this passage is Jesus' resurrection, the foundation of the Christian faith. The resurrection shows Jesus' victory over death, confirms His divinity, and brings all believers the hope of eternal life. The angel's message, "He is not here, for He has risen," is direct confirmation of Jesus' own prophecy that He would rise from the dead.

Through this passage God shows us that whatever challenges or difficulties arise in our lives, victory and hope are always possible. Jesus' resurrection encourages us to believe that God has the power to change any situation, and that even death cannot stop His plan.
q: When you face difficulty or setbacks in life, how does Jesus' resurrection bring you hope? How can you share this resurrection hope with the people around you?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for showing us, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, the power that overcomes death and despair. Give us faith, so that when we face the challenges and trials of life, we may firmly believe in Your salvation and the power of the resurrection. On our journey, keep reminding us that You are always with us, leading us toward light and hope. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: As they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Rejoice!” They came and took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
Then Jesus said to them, “Don’t be afraid. Go tell my brothers  that they should go into Galilee, and there they will see me.”
Now while they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city, and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.
When they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave a large amount of silver to the soldiers,
saying, “Say that his disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.
If this comes to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him and make you free of worry.”
So they took the money and did as they were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.
b: This passage describes the first meeting of the risen Jesus with His disciples, especially the women who followed Him. When Jesus appeared to them and greeted them, "Rejoice!" ("Peace to you"), they felt great joy and fear. Jesus not only comforted them, telling them not to be afraid, but also commanded them to go and tell the other disciples that He had risen and would meet them in Galilee.

The passage also reveals how the authorities tried to cover up the truth. When the soldiers who guarded the tomb went back into the city to report what had happened, the chief priests and elders gave them money and instructed them to spread the rumor that Jesus' body had been stolen by His disciples. This shows not only the corruption and deceit of the religious and political leaders, but also people's resistance to the truth.

Through this passage God reveals to us that even in adversity and doubt, the light of truth cannot be hidden. Jesus' resurrection is not only a victory over death but also an exposure of every lie and conspiracy. Jesus encourages us not to be afraid, but to live boldly and bear witness to His truth and love.
q: When you meet injustice or misunderstanding in life, how do you hold on to and proclaim God's truth? How do you keep a peaceful heart in those situations?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that through the resurrection of Jesus Christ You have given us power over fear and unbelief. Help us, when we face the challenges of life, to hold to the truth and not fear the threat of lies. Give us courage to witness for Your Kingdom not only in safe settings but also amid opposition and difficulty. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
When they saw him, they bowed down to him, but some doubted.
Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
b: This passage is known as the "Great Commission," Jesus Christ's final instruction to His disciples and a mission for all believers. Jesus directed His disciples to a mountain in Galilee, where He gave them authority and issued the call to worldwide mission. This instruction shows that all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Jesus, and so He authorizes His disciples to carry out His command.

Jesus asks His disciples to "go and make disciples of all nations." This is not a simple task of passing on information, but a process of teaching, baptizing, and nurturing spiritual life. In addition, Jesus' command includes baptizing in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, which underscores the core doctrine of the Trinity in the Christian faith.

Jesus' promise, "Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age," gives believers comfort and assurance as they carry out the mission. These words are not only a promise but also a guarantee of continual support and divine presence for believers.

Through this passage God shows us that as followers of Christ we are called to live out and proclaim the gospel to every corner of the world. Wherever we are, we should take Jesus' teaching as the guide for our lives and take an active part in the work of bringing people to Christ.
q: In your daily life, how can you more actively fulfill Jesus' Great Commission? In what specific actions can you show your commitment to world mission?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving us, through Your Son Jesus Christ, this great mission of making all nations Your disciples. Give us wisdom and courage to bear witness to Your love and truth through Your word and our lives. Help us remember that wherever we go, You are with us, to the end of the age. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in the prophets, “Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you:
the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord! Make his paths straight!’ ”
John came baptizing in the wilderness and preaching the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem went out to him. They were baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.
John was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
He preached, saying, “After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and loosen.
I baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”
b: 這段經文講述了耶穌基督福音的開端，並強調了施洗約翰作為主的前鋒，為耶穌的來臨預備道路的重要角色。約翰在曠野中呼籲人們悔改並接受洗禮，這不僅象徵著內心的潔淨，也為將來耶穌的到來打下了基礎。約翰的傳道生活極其簡樸，他穿著駱駝毛的衣服，吃蝗蟲和野蜜，這樣的生活方式象徵著他的純潔和完全獻身於神的使命。
經文的核心是約翰的傳道信息，他說：「有一位在我以後來的，能力比我更大，我就是彎腰給他解鞋帶也是不配的。」這句話顯示了約翰的謙卑，他認識到自己不過是為耶穌作鋪路的人，而耶穌則是那位真正能以聖靈施洗的主。
上帝透過這段經文向我們傳達了一個重要的信息：我們每一個人都需要預備自己的心來迎接耶穌的到來。這不僅僅是外在的行為改變，更是內心的悔改和靈性的更新。就如同約翰為耶穌的來臨預備道路，我們也被召喚來在我們的生活中為主預備道路，使我們的生命成為承載神的旨意和祝福的器皿。
q: 在您的生活中，是否有需要悔改的地方，以便更好地為主預備道路？您願意如何實際地讓耶穌在您的生活中掌權？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您藉著施洗約翰的榜樣，提醒我們預備心靈來迎接耶穌的到來。求您幫助我們每天都能以謙卑和悔改的心來尋求您，並在我們的生活中彰顯您的愛和真理。願我們的生命成為您福音的見證，榮耀您的名。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
Immediately coming up from the water, he saw the heavens parting, and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.
A voice came out of the sky, “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.
He was there in the wilderness forty days tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals; and the angels were serving him.
b: 這段經文講述了耶穌基督在祂公開事工開始之前的兩個關鍵事件，並揭示了祂的身份和使命的核心。首先，耶穌從加利利的拿撒勒來到約旦河，接受施洗約翰的洗禮。這個時刻非常重要，因為它象徵著耶穌正式進入祂的救贖事工。當耶穌從水中上來時，天開了，這是一個神聖的象徵，表明神與人類的直接接觸。聖靈如鴿子降在耶穌身上，代表著聖靈的同在和引導。而天上的聲音「你是我的愛子，我喜悅你」清楚地確立了耶穌的身份——祂是神的愛子，並且祂所做的一切都是蒙神喜悅的。
接著，聖靈把耶穌帶到曠野，祂在那裡經歷了四十天的試探。曠野常常象徵著試煉和屬靈的鍛煉，耶穌的四十天正如以色列人在曠野的四十年一樣，是一段屬靈淨化和試煉的時期。在這段期間，耶穌面對撒但的試探，這些試探考驗了祂對神的順服和信心。然而，耶穌並沒有孤單一人地面對這些挑戰，因為天使在祂身邊伺候祂，這表明神的保護和供應永遠不會離開祂。

上帝透過這段經文向我們顯示了幾個深刻的真理。首先，耶穌的洗禮提醒我們，雖然祂本無罪，卻願意與我們認同，進入我們的世界，為我們的罪而死。我們每個人也都需要經歷屬靈的洗禮，這不僅是外在的象徵，更是內在的悔改和重生。其次，耶穌在曠野的試探教導我們，即便我們面臨最大的試探和挑戰，神依然與我們同在，聖靈會賜給我們力量來勝過這些試探。神已經確認了我們的身份，正如祂對耶穌所說的「你是我的愛子，我喜悅你」，我們也是祂所愛的兒女，蒙祂的喜悅，並受祂的保護和引導。
q: 在您生命的旅程中，是否有些時刻感到像是在曠野中面對試探和孤單？在這些時刻，您如何更深地依靠聖靈的引導和神的力量？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您藉著耶穌基督的榜樣，讓我們看見在試探和挑戰中依然能夠堅持信心的力量。求您幫助我們在面對人生的曠野時，能夠像耶穌一樣，倚靠聖靈的引導，戰勝撒但的試探。讓我們不斷記得，我們是您所愛的兒女，並在每一天的生活中顯明您的榮耀。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Good News of God’s Kingdom,
and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”
Passing along by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, the brother of Simon, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”
Immediately they left their nets, and followed him.
Going on a little further from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets.
Immediately he called them, and they left their father, Zebedee, in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.
b: 這段經文記載了耶穌開始祂公開事工的關鍵時刻，以及祂招募門徒的過程。約翰下監之後，耶穌在加利利開始宣講福音，祂的信息簡潔有力：「日期滿了，神的國近了。你們當悔改，信福音！」這一宣告標誌著神國度的臨近，並呼召人們回轉歸向神。
耶穌在呼召門徒時，選擇了普通的漁夫西門、安得烈、雅各和約翰。祂邀請他們來跟從祂，並告訴他們，他們將成為「得人如得魚」的使者。這個比喻生動地描繪了他們未來使命的性質：他們將不再是為了自己的生計而打魚，而是要成為神國的使者，把人們帶進神的國度。
這段經文特別強調了即時的跟從與捨棄，西門和安得烈立刻捨了網，跟從耶穌；雅各和約翰也同樣捨棄了家庭和職業，順服耶穌的呼召。他們的回應展示了信仰的立即性和完全委身的特質，這也是每一位跟從基督的人應當具備的態度。
上帝透過這段經文教導我們：神的呼召是強而有力且充滿恩典的。當我們聽到神的聲音時，我們應當毫不猶豫地回應，並願意捨棄一切來跟從祂。這不僅僅是外在行為的改變，更是心靈深處的轉變，從追求世俗的目標轉向追隨永恆的價值。神呼召我們去「得人如得魚」，成為祂福音的見證人，在這世界中為祂的國度作工。
q: 當您聽到神的呼召時，您是否願意立刻回應並跟從祂？在您的生活中，有什麼需要捨棄的，以更好地跟隨主？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您召喚我們成為您國度的子民，並賜給我們成為您福音使者的使命。求您賜我們勇氣和力量，使我們能夠像那些門徒一樣，立刻回應您的呼召，並將我們的生命全然獻上。讓我們每天都能聽到您的聲音，並在生活中實踐您的旨意。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.
They were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as having authority, and not as the scribes.
Immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
saying, “Ha! What do we have to do with you, Jesus, you Nazarene? Have you come to destroy us? I know you who you are: the Holy One of God!”
Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be quiet, and come out of him!”
The unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying with a loud voice, came out of him.
They were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, “What is this? A new teaching? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him!”
The report of him went out immediately everywhere into all the region of Galilee and its surrounding area.
Immediately, when they had come out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Now Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her.
He came and took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her immediately, and she served them.
At evening, when the sun had set, they brought to him all who were sick, and those who were possessed by demons.
All the city was gathered together at the door.
He healed many who were sick with various diseases, and cast out many demons. He didn’t allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.
b: 這段經文詳細記載了耶穌在迦百農的事工，並展現了祂的教導和神蹟的權柄。耶穌在安息日進入會堂教訓人，眾人對祂的教訓感到驚奇，因為祂教訓他們像是有權柄的人，而不是像文士那樣單純地解釋律法。這表明耶穌的話語充滿了神的權威，祂不僅僅是解釋經文，而是以創造者和立法者的身份來教導人。
在會堂中，耶穌遇到了一個被污鬼附著的人，這人認出了耶穌是「神的聖者」，並害怕祂來滅他們。耶穌用權柄命令污鬼出來，並不許他們再作聲。這顯示了耶穌對邪靈的絕對控制和勝過黑暗勢力的能力。
耶穌離開會堂後，進入西門的家，祂治好了西門的岳母，使她立刻能夠起來服事他們。當天晚些時候，許多患病和被鬼附的人都來到耶穌跟前，祂一一治好了他們，並且趕出許多鬼。耶穌不許鬼說話，因為鬼認識祂的真實身份。
上帝透過這段經文教導我們：耶穌基督是擁有絕對權柄的主，祂的話語和作為都充滿了神的力量。無論是在教導中還是在行神蹟時，耶穌都顯明了祂的神性和權威。這提醒我們，在我們的生活中，無論面對什麼樣的挑戰或試探，我們都可以完全信靠耶穌，因為祂已勝過一切黑暗勢力，並賜給我們新的生命。
q: 當您面對生活中的困難或屬靈的爭戰時，您是否完全信靠耶穌的權柄和能力？在什麼情境下，您需要更多地依靠祂的幫助？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您藉著耶穌基督顯示出祂的權柄和能力，祂不僅能夠教導我們真理，還能夠醫治我們的身心靈。求您幫助我們在生活中信靠祂，無論面對何種困難或黑暗，都能倚靠祂的力量得勝。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and went out, and departed into a deserted place, and prayed there.
Simon and those who were with him searched for him.
They found him and told him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
He said to them, “Let’s go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because I came out for this reason.”
He went into their synagogues throughout all Galilee, preaching and casting out demons.
b: 這段經文描繪了耶穌在早晨的禱告生活和祂的傳道使命。耶穌在清晨時分，獨自前往曠野地方禱告，這顯示了祂對與天父溝通的重視和祈禱的必須性。祂在禱告中尋求神的指引和力量，以完成祂的使命。
西門和他的同伴找到耶穌，告訴祂眾人都在尋找祂，顯示了耶穌在群眾中的影響力。然而，耶穌沒有被這些人的期望所吸引，祂知道自己的使命是去各地傳道，並且要把福音帶給更多的人。祂在祂的使命中展現了堅定的目標和清晰的方向。
耶穌的回答表明，祂的傳道工作不僅限於一個地方，而是要擴展到更廣的範圍。耶穌周遊各城，傳講神的國度，並且趕鬼，彰顯了祂對人類靈魂的關懷和祂的大能。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，禱告和與神的溝通是我們靈命生活的重要部分，並且我們的使命是要擴展神的國度，向更多人分享福音。耶穌的榜樣告訴我們，在忙碌和需求中，我們也應該尋求神的指引，保持我們的使命感。
q: 在您的日常生活中，您如何能夠更好地安排時間來禱告，並尋求神的指引？您是否清楚自己的使命，並在生活中努力實踐？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您示範了禱告和使命的重要性。求您幫助我們在忙碌的生活中，也能夠像耶穌一樣，保持與您的親密關係，尋求您的指引。願我們的生活能夠反映出我們對您使命的忠誠，並且願意向更多人分享您的福音。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: A leper came to him, begging him, kneeling down to him, and saying to him, “If you want to, you can make me clean.”
Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”
When he had said this, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was made clean.
He strictly warned him, and immediately sent him out,
and said to him, “See you say nothing to anybody, but go show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing the things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”

But he went out, and began to proclaim it much, and to spread about the matter, so that Jesus could no more openly enter into a city, but was outside in desert places. People came to him from everywhere.
b: 這段經文講述了耶穌醫治一位痲瘋病人的故事。痲瘋病人在猶太社會中被視為不潔，他們被孤立於社會之外，與家人、社區隔絕，過著痛苦的生活。然而，這位病人冒著極大的風險來到耶穌面前，表達出對耶穌醫治大能的絕對信任。他向耶穌說：「你若肯，必能叫我潔淨了。」這句話顯示了他深深的信心，他相信耶穌有能力醫治他，關鍵在於耶穌是否願意。
耶穌的回應讓人感動。祂不僅用話語醫治了這位病人，還主動伸手觸摸了他。這個動作在當時是非常特別的，因為觸摸痲瘋病人會被認為是不潔的，但耶穌不受這些社會規範的束縛，祂以無條件的愛接納這位病人，並說：「我肯，你潔淨了吧！」這句話不僅表達了耶穌的願意，更顯示出祂醫治的權柄。結果，痲瘋病人立刻得到潔淨，這表明耶穌的醫治是即時且完全的。
然而，耶穌並不希望這件事被廣泛宣揚，祂囑咐病人不要告訴他人，只要求他按律法去祭司那裡檢查並獻上禮物。然而，這位病人無法壓抑內心的喜悅，將這奇蹟告訴了更多的人，導致耶穌不得不離開城鎮，在曠野中活動。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，無論我們的情況多麼困難，祂都有能力醫治和拯救我們。耶穌的慈愛和憐憫不僅僅停留在話語上，祂的行動也證明了祂的愛。祂願意觸摸我們生命中最不潔的部分，並以祂的恩典使我們得潔淨。這也呼喚我們去信靠祂，將我們的困境交託給祂，因為祂願意且有能力改變我們的生命。
q: 在您的生命中，是否有哪個領域需要耶穌的醫治和潔淨？您願意以信心來到祂面前，將這些重擔交託給祂嗎？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您藉著耶穌基督向我們顯明無條件的愛與醫治大能。求您幫助我們在困境中能夠像痲瘋病人一樣，帶著信心來到您面前，尋求您的幫助和醫治。願我們在得著您恩典的同時，也能成為他人的祝福，將您的愛傳遞出去。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: When he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was heard that he was in the house.
Immediately many were gathered together, so that there was no more room, not even around the door; and he spoke the word to them.
Four people came, carrying a paralytic to him.
When they could not come near to him for the crowd, they removed the roof where he was. When they had broken it up, they let down the mat that the paralytic was lying on.
Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”
But there were some of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,
“Why does this man speak blasphemies like that? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
Immediately Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, said to them, “Why do you reason these things in your hearts?
Which is easier, to tell the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Arise, and take up your bed, and walk?’
But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—
“I tell you, arise, take up your mat, and go to your house.”
He arose, and immediately took up the mat, and went out in front of them all; so that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, “We never saw anything like this!”
b: 這段經文描述了耶穌在迦百農醫治一位癱子的故事，這奇蹟展現了耶穌的權柄，不僅在於祂能夠醫治疾病，還在於祂擁有赦罪的權柄。這位癱子的朋友們展現了非凡的信心，他們不顧一切地將癱子抬到耶穌面前，甚至拆開房頂，這樣的行動顯示了他們對耶穌能力的全然信賴。
耶穌在這個場景中首先宣告了癱子的罪得赦，這個舉動讓周圍的文士感到震驚，因為在他們看來，只有神有權赦罪。然而，耶穌藉著這次醫治，不僅顯示出祂的醫治大能，也公開宣告了祂是神的兒子，擁有赦罪的權柄。最終，癱子當眾站立行走，這不僅醫治了他的身體，也顯明了耶穌的神性和祂救贖的大能。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，信心是通往神蹟的關鍵，我們需要像這些朋友一樣，不顧一切障礙，將我們的需要帶到耶穌面前。此外，我們要認識到耶穌的救贖不僅僅在於身體的醫治，更重要的是祂能夠赦免我們的罪，帶給我們真正的自由和新的生命。

v: He went out again by the seaside. All the multitude came to him, and he taught them.
As he passed by, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office, and he said to him, “Follow me.” And he arose and followed him.
He was reclining at the table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.
The scribes and the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, “Why is it that he eats and drinks with tax collectors and sinners?”
When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
b: 這段經文描述了耶穌呼召稅吏利未成為祂的門徒，並且與他和其他稅吏、罪人一同坐席的故事。利未（即馬太）是稅吏，在猶太社會中被視為叛徒和不潔之人，因為他們替羅馬政府收稅，並且經常利用職位中飽私囊。儘管如此，耶穌並沒有因為利未的社會地位和過去的行為而拒絕他，反而主動呼召他跟從自己。
耶穌的行动挑戰了當時的宗教領袖和社會常規。當法利賽人質疑耶穌為何與罪人和稅吏一同吃喝時，耶穌回應道：「康健的人用不著醫生，有病的人才用得著。我來本不是召義人，乃是召罪人。」這句話表明了耶穌的使命，祂來到世上不是為了那些自認為無罪的義人，而是為了那些承認自己有罪並需要救恩的人。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，祂的愛和救恩是無條件的，不論我們過去如何，只要我們願意悔改並跟隨祂，祂就會接納我們。耶穌的呼召超越了社會的標籤和偏見，祂願意與那些被社會排斥的人同席，並賜給他們新的生命。

v: John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came and asked him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples don’t fast?”
Jesus said to them, “Can the groomsmen fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they can’t fast.
But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast in that day.
No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made.
No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins will be destroyed; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins.”
b: 這段經文中，耶穌被質疑為何祂的門徒不遵守禁食的傳統，而祂的回答揭示了祂所帶來的新時代。耶穌將自己比作新郎，表示祂的來臨是一個充滿喜樂的時刻，因此祂的門徒不需要禁食，因為禁食通常是表達悲傷和悔改的行為。耶穌指出，當祂不在時，門徒才會禁食，這表明了祂對祂即將到來的苦難和離別的預告。
耶穌進一步用新布和舊衣服、新酒和舊皮袋的比喻來說明，祂帶來的是全新的教導和恩典，這些新事物無法與舊有的律法和傳統相兼容。就像新布會扯壞舊衣服，新酒會裂開舊皮袋一樣，耶穌的教導要求我們有新的心態和生命來承接祂所帶來的改變。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，當我們接受耶穌基督的救恩時，我們的生命必須經歷一個全新的轉變。我們不能用舊有的思維方式和生活方式來應對神的新恩典，而是要以更新的心靈來迎接祂的工作。這也挑戰我們放下過去的束縛，敞開心扉迎接神所賜的新生命。

v: He was going on the Sabbath day through the grain fields, and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, “Behold, why do they do that which is not lawful on the Sabbath day?”
He said to them, “Did you never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry—he, and those who were with him?
How he entered into God’s house at the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the show bread, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those who were with him?”
He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
b: 這段經文中，耶穌和祂的門徒在安息日行路，掐了麥穗，這引發了法利賽人的不滿，因為在他們眼中，這樣的行為違反了安息日的規範。然而，耶穌並不受這些律法束縛，祂用大衛在飢餓時吃陳設餅的例子來回應他們，表明在神的眼中，人的需要超越了律法的細節。
耶穌的話語「安息日是為人設立的，人不是為安息日設立的」揭示了神設立律法的本意。律法的目的是為了保護人、祝福人，而不是束縛人。耶穌進一步宣告自己是安息日的主，這表明祂擁有詮釋律法的權柄，並且祂的權柄超越了律法本身。耶穌來到世上，帶來了真正的安息，這種安息並不在於外在的形式，而在於與神的和好與靈魂的平安。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，不要讓律法和規範成為我們與神之間的障礙。耶穌來到世上，祂的教導超越了律法的字句，將我們引向與神的真實關係。我們不應該被律法的重擔壓垮，而是要在耶穌基督裡找到真正的自由和安息。
